- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (high sentiment > 0.67) — model tends to overshoot early in uptrends.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment (sentiment < 0.33) — model fails to capture sharp reversals or bottoming.
- Lag in price response: model often lags true price movements by 2–3 days, especially after sentiment shifts.
- Overshoot after spikes: model overreacts to recent price spikes, leading to inflated forecasts in the following days.
- Mean reversion bias: model underestimates long-term mean reversion in high volatility periods, especially when sentiment is mixed.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts are consistently too high in early periods (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is rising, then adjust downward later.
- Sentiment-weighted correction: if sentiment > 0.7, reduce forecast by 2–5% to avoid overconfidence; if sentiment < 0.3, increase forecast by 3–7% to compensate for underreaction.
